text: Figure 6.1: Communication with MKA Module in AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. If a Host has the architecture of the previous drawing, the following actions happen until the Host sends the first MACsec protected frame. • Kernel startup: the physical interfaces are detected and the driver is initialized. • Initialization of the network configuration: configuration of the Phy/Switch (Link Speed, MACsec enabling, . . .), setup of VLANs (Virtual VLAN interfaces are created) and configuration of MACsec bypass rules in the Phy/Switch (Bypassed VLANs, Ethertype 0x88E5, MKA). At this point, the interfaces which does not use MACsec (eth0, eth0.34, eth1 and eth1.45 on the figure) have already signaled a link up. The rest signal a link down. • Launch MKA Daemon: generate virtual MACsec interfaces as defined in the configuration files: – eth0 → macsec0 (down) – macsec0.12 (down) (virtual VLAN interface over macsec0) – macsec0.23 (down) (virtual VLAN interface over macsec0) • Launch of non-MACsec stacks/Daemons (Communication Management, Adaptive Applications, . . .). From this moment, non-protected frames can be sent through the unprotected adapters.
